_meta.source: Seal Cascade campaign — hand-authored in campaign voice, grounded in the campaign vault (BigZ's Vault/Game Design/Ragnarok_Online) and arc scripts
_meta.note: Highest merge priority in the bestiary Scholar tier (campaign > RML > Fandom). Covers campaign-referenced mobs no external source documents. Spoiler-calibrated: entries foreshadow arc themes but do not reveal hidden twists.

1366.title: Lava Golem
1366.lore: The magma under Veins does not cool the way rock should, and where it pools too long it stands up. Lava golems are slag given a walking shape — miners call them 'firebreaks' with bitter humor, because every one that crosses a gallery leaves a burning seam behind it. Since the deep shift began they wander farther from the vents than the old-timers have ever seen. Water quenches the shell; the core stays hot enough to reignite for hours.

1417.title: Zipper Bear
1417.lore: A squat black bear of the eastern hills with a mouth that closes like a drawstring purse — and opens wide enough to take a lantern whole. Einbroch's mine-surgeons pay standing bounties for their gall: rendered down, it is the only remedy that loosens coal dust from a miner's lungs. The bears know the shift whistles better than the miners do, and forage the tailings when the tunnels empty.

1503.title: Gibbet
1503.lore: In Niflheim's Banquet Hall the Gibbet do not haunt the city — they are part of its architecture, the way a keystone is part of a bridge. Hanged shapes that sway from nothing, older than any of the recently dead, set in their places when the pale city first set its tables. The overflow pouring across death's border has unsettled even them, and an unsettled Gibbet leaves its appointed place. The dead of Niflheim find this alarming. The living should too.

1506.title: Disguise
1506.lore: It has no face of its own, so it borrows. The Disguise is a rag of spirit that drapes itself in the recently seen — a footman's coat, a diplomat's smile, a friend's walk — always slightly wrong, like a portrait painted from a description. At a crowded banquet it is not one guest; it is any of them. Watch the wine: a Disguise raises its glass on the wrong beat, because it toasts to what the room feels, not what it hears.

1507.title: Bloody Murderer
1507.lore: Some killers are executed and stop. This one was executed and continued — a butcher's ghost that still keeps a professional's schedule, dragging its chained cleaver through halls it was never invited to. It does not rage; it works. Witnesses who survive describe the same detail: it pauses to wipe the blade between victims, as if the next cut deserves a clean edge. In fine company it has no manners at all, only appointments.

1509.title: Lude
1509.lore: A small hooded ghost, all sleeve and shuffle, that trails the overflow of the dead like a child following a parade it does not understand. Ludes are the least of the unquiet — the recently, mildly, apologetically dead — and they are drawn to warmth, lamplight, and being counted. Scholars of the pale city insist a Lude cannot hurt you. This is true. It can, however, lead you somewhere that will.

1510.title: Hylozoist
1510.lore: The old heresy held that all matter is alive and only politeness keeps it still. The Hylozoist is what happens when something believes the heresy hard enough to enforce it. In the tower where memory outlived its maker, these stitched shapes move through the halls waking things that should not wake — a chair, a door, a suit of armor, a grief. Kill the doll and the animation stops; the belief, unfortunately, is load-bearing in that place.

1511.title: Amon Ra
1511.lore: The god-king under the Pyramid was not buried; he was installed. Morroc's oldest dynasties built downward, dynasty under dynasty, until the deepest chamber — and set Amon Ra in it as king, warden, and threshold all at once. He rises crowned in gold and judgment, attended by the scarab-dead, and the air behind his throne blows cold from somewhere no map admits exists. Grave-robbers call his chamber the bottom of the Pyramid. The kings who built it knew better.

1583.title: Tao Gunka
1583.lore: Past Byalan the sea floor drops into a trench the charts leave decently blank, and in it something the size of an island has been asleep longer than Alberta has had docks. The fishermen knew the rule without being taught: nothing heavy goes over the trench. Then the crates went in anyway, and the nets began coming up empty — or screaming. Tao Gunka is stone-white, tide-slow, and patient the way only the very large can afford to be. It is climbing toward the light now. Ask what woke it *after* it is dead.

1676.title: Venatu
1676.lore: The builders of Juperos are gone; their staff, regrettably, is not. Venatu are custodial automatons still executing the final standing order of a city that died mid-shift — patrol, inspect, remove obstruction. Rust has not slowed the removal step. They nest thickest around shafts and conduits that lead to what the city was built to hold, which is why every extraction crew that goes down for salvage learns the same lesson: the machines are not guarding treasure. They are guarding *procedure*.

1715.title: Novus
1715.lore: A Novus is a dragon the way a spark is a fire — juvenile, quick, and mostly appetite, wings still too big for its judgment. They shoal like fish over the deep water east of Hugel, which is the detail worth losing sleep over: dragons do not school by nature. Something below the lake has them packing together and staying up where the light is. Cull the packs if the farms demand it, but note which way the young ones refuse to fly.

1775.title: Snowier
1775.lore: A drift that prays. Snowiers pile themselves into rough kneeling shapes along the ice caves beneath the holy city, hollow at the core — pilgrims swear the wind through that hollow sounds like the responses in a temple service, half a beat behind. The faithful call them blessed and leave offerings. The offerings are always gone by morning. Whatever fills the hollow when no one is watching, it is heavier than snow: their tracks compress solid ice.

1777.title: Ice Titan
1777.lore: The glacier under Rachel's temple does not calve; it *walks*, one titan at a time. An Ice Titan is old compression given limbs — centuries of snowfall pressed until it remembers pressure as a kind of will. At its center hangs a core of ice so dense it bends lamplight, and it is these cores the temple quietly pays to have sampled, as if someone up there is dating exactly how old the cold beneath their sanctuary is. The titans object to the coring. Slowly. Then all at once.

1782.title: Roween
1782.lore: The wild dogs of the Einbroch fields were ordinary once, before the smokestacks taught them new hours. Roween packs run on factory time now — they gather at the shift whistle, when the gates open and the tired walk home alone through the ash-fields. Soot-gray, lean, and patient, they have learned that the city feeds them best at the change of shift. The foremen post the walk-home roster in pairs for a reason.

1832.title: Ifrit
1832.lore: Beneath Thor's Volcano sleeps the fire that ends the world, and Ifrit is its herald — woken not to fight but to *announce*. A crowned elemental of chained flame, it rises through the magma galleries proclaiming, in a tongue older than the volcano, the dimensions of what follows it. No mortal at any attainable strength faces what it heralds. But heralds can be silenced, and in the reading of a dead herald's embers the wise may learn exactly how large the end intends to be — and how long is left to argue with it.

1865.title: Ragged Zombie
1865.lore: The abbey on the island with no name buried its dead with bells — a cord in every coffin, a bell above every grave, mercy against the old fear of waking underground. The Ragged Zombies are the ones who rang and were not dug up. They shamble in the rotted habits of the order that abandoned them, and they still gather when the abbey bells sound, obedient to the last rule they ever kept. Whoever holds the bell rotation holds the graveyard.

1992.title: Cornus
1992.lore: On the far side of the crossing, where the light falls at an angle Midgard's sun never taught it, the Cornus graze — laurel-winged unicorns the Sapha treat as sacred and the Laphine as omens. The crossing sickens them: the passage that brought Midgard's expeditions through leaks something the herds cannot metabolize, and the afflicted turn glass-eyed and violent before the end. The mercy runs exist because the Sapha cannot bear to do it themselves, and cannot bear to let it go undone.

1993.title: Naga
1993.lore: The serpent-folk of the new world's marches owe allegiance to neither great people and have outlasted every border drawn across their wetlands. Naga fight the way rivers fight — yielding ground, coiling around what enters, drowning it at leisure. They watch the crossing with an attention the diplomats find uncomfortable, because the Naga are old enough here to remember whether anything came through it *before*. They are not saying. Their spears say they were not surprised.

2223.title: Celia
2223.lore: In the inner corridors of the buried biosphere, the Administrator's security still walks its rounds wearing a woman's face. The Celia-pattern constructs are courteous, symmetrical, and wrong in the way a reflection is wrong — a defense layer built to be mistaken for staff until the moment of enforcement. Each carries a fraction of the facility's old authority: doors obey them, lights follow them, and the outer labs' escaped subjects flee at the sound of their even, unhurried footsteps.

2398.title: Little Poring
2398.lore: Even Prontera's gentlest export has an off-season. Little Porings swarm the fountain plaza in numbers no forager can explain, bouncing underfoot in a mood the city's children call playful and the Sigil Ring calls something else — a low, cheerful pressure, the same overflow the party learned to read as the cascade's earliest tremor. They are harmless alone. In a crowd this size, harmless stops being reassuring.

1290.title: Skeleton General
1290.lore: The bone-fields past Payon buried common soldiers by the thousand, and one grave in a hundred remembers rank. A Skeleton General still marshals — raises a rusted blade in signal, and the lesser dead nearby straighten their line before they attack. Payon's tomb-guides say the generals don't know the war ended; they know only that the whistle hasn't blown to stand down, and no living officer has come to give the order.

1301.title: Am Mut
1301.lore: A jackal-headed watcher out of the desert's oldest stories, said to weigh a traveler's heart against a feather at the threshold of the dead. In Payon's outer sands the Am Mut has forgotten the ceremony and kept only the appetite — it still confronts anyone who crosses its ground, still judges, but the verdict is no longer in question. Rashid warns new parties not to mistake its patience for mercy; it is only being thorough.

1307.title: Cat o' Nine Tails
1307.lore: Nine fox-spirits sharing one body, or one spirit wearing nine faces — Payon's grove-folk argue the point and agree on the danger. It moves like a shrug, all its tails flicking a different direction at once, and no two witnesses describe the same face as the one that struck them. The shrine-mediums treat it as an omen of a choice not yet made: nine possible paths, and the cat has not decided which one to close.

1297.title: Ancient Mummy
1297.lore: Morroc's sand keeps its dead honest — wrapped, sealed, and shelved in the pyramid's lower galleries long before the dynasty that built Amon Ra's chamber ever cut stone. An Ancient Mummy does not shamble like the recently raised; it processes, unhurried, wrappings trailing curse-dust that outlives its wearer's patience. Tomb-guides rate them lower on the danger scale than the fresher dead, on the grounds that at least a mummy is predictable. They are also, usually, right.

1314.title: Permeter
1314.lore: The turtle-dungeon beneath Izlude keeps three elemental wardens turning in an old rotation, and Permeter is the ground's turn — a stone-plated tortoise slow enough to mistake for terrain until the floor itself seems to attack. Sailors call the dungeon's cycling wardens 'the argument,' because Permeter, Heater, and Freezer have never agreed on which element should own the depths, and something down there keeps refusing to let any of them win outright.

1318.title: Heater
1318.lore: The second warden of Izlude's turtle-dungeon rotation, shell glowing coal-red, patrolling galleries that stay warm long after it passes. Divers who've mapped the depths note that Heater never strays into Freezer's territory and Freezer never strays into Heater's — an old boundary neither warden seems able to cross, as if something set the lines before either of them had an opinion about it.

1319.title: Freezer
1319.lore: Where Heater's galleries run warm, Freezer's run cold enough to fog a diver's lamp — the turtle-dungeon's third warden, patient and armored in frost that never quite melts even this close to the volcanic vents nearby. Local legend holds that the three wardens (Permeter, Heater, Freezer) were sealed here to keep something older and unaligned from picking an element at all. Nobody has confirmed what. Nobody has gone deep enough to ask.

1615.title: Obsidian
1615.lore: Einbroch's coal seams run deep enough to compress more than rock, and Obsidian is what the mine calls the results — a glass-black golem of fused slag and pressure that wanders the tunnels the smelters have long since abandoned. Miners treat an Obsidian sighting as a schedule change, not an emergency: it doesn't chase, it doesn't hurry, and it has never once left the deep galleries where the company stopped keeping records.

1623.title: RSX-0806
1623.lore: Einbroch built RSX-0806 to end a war and then buried it when the war ended, filed under an asset-tracking number instead of a name. It should still be off. Someone with Rekenber clearance turned the key anyway and used the reactivation bay — and the city's own workers — as a live-fire test. What the party finds when it falls is worse than the machine: a data trail running straight to Lighthalzen, where Rekenber has stopped building weapons around people and started building people as weapons.

1778.title: Gazeti
1778.lore: The ice caves under Rachel host more than praying drifts and glacier-titans — Gazeti are the caves' smaller, quicker cold, spined things that move in the dark between the ice pillars where a lantern doesn't reach. Pilgrims rarely see one directly; they notice the cold spot first, then the spines, and by then a Gazeti has already decided whether the intrusion is worth the trouble of chasing.

1789.title: Iceicle
1789.lore: A shard of the Rachel glacier that decided to keep moving after it broke off — Iceicle drifts through the ice caves at a pace that looks accidental until it changes direction to follow something warm. The temple's cold-caretakers consider them a nuisance rather than a threat, though they concede the nuisance has teeth, and that the caves have been calving more of them since the titans started walking farther than usual.

2221.title: Randel
2221.lore: Lighthalzen's Bio Labs kept a research staff long after the last legitimate project closed, and Randel is what's left of one — reshaped by whatever Rekenber's later experiments required, still moving through the wards on a schedule only he remembers setting. The Prometheus files name him, Flamel, Chen, Gertie, Alphoccio, and Trentini as a single cohort: six researchers who went in to study the process and came out as part of it.

2222.title: Flamel
2222.lore: One of the six Bio Lab researchers the Prometheus Project consumed rather than employed. Flamel's notes, what survive of them, describe a fascination with transmutation that the labs were happy to indulge — until the indulging stopped being metaphorical. What patrols the wards now still moves like someone taking careful notes, just without a hand left steady enough to hold the pen.

2224.title: Chen
2224.lore: Chen was Bio Lab security once, brought in to keep the six researchers' work contained. The containment failed in both directions: nothing stayed in, and Chen didn't stay Chen. What remains still patrols with a guard's instinct for chokepoints and blind corners, which makes the wards more dangerous, not less, for anyone who assumes the change left the training behind too.

2225.title: Gertie
2225.lore: The gentlest name among the six consumed researchers, and by every account the gentlest person — which is exactly why the surviving lab logs single her out as the loss that finally turned the rest of the staff against the Prometheus Project, decades before Rekenber decided to restart it anyway. What moves through the wards now doesn't recognize the objection it once raised.

2226.title: Alphoccio
2226.lore: Of the six Bio Lab researchers folded into the Prometheus Project, Alphoccio's notes show the least resistance and the most enthusiasm — a scientist who kept documenting the process on himself past the point anyone could call it professional curiosity. The wards remember his handwriting getting worse across the file. They don't say what he was still trying to write down at the end.

2227.title: Trentini
2227.lore: The last-hired of the six consumed researchers, and the one whose personnel file Rekenber tried hardest to lose. Trentini's role in the Prometheus Project was oversight — sent to audit the others, not join them. Whatever now patrols the wards under that name is either the audit's final finding or its final casualty, and Lighthalzen's surviving records don't agree on which.

1699.title: Ancient Mimic
1699.lore: Hugel's dragon-nest caverns hold treasure old enough that even the trickery guarding it has fossilized — an Ancient Mimic sits heavier and slower than its city cousins, having long since stopped needing to move fast when nothing has disturbed its hoard in a generation. Wardens who've catalogued the nest note it's the one 'chest' in the caverns worth checking twice before worth opening once.

1713.title: Acidus
1713.lore: A juvenile of the Hugel dragon-nest, half-formed and corrosive before its scales properly set — Acidus spits a caustic ichor in place of the fire its elders will eventually breathe, the nest's way of arming its young before they're strong enough to fight conventionally. Wardens who cull the nest for the farms below always leave the eldest clutches; it's the young, unpredictable broods like this one that actually stray.

1714.title: Ferus
1714.lore: Ferus are Hugel's dragon-nest hatchlings a season past Acidus — faster, meaner, and just old enough to hunt in the caverns' upper galleries instead of waiting to be fed. The nest wardens track their numbers more closely than any other brood, since a Ferus that leaves the nest healthy tends to come back leading younger siblings, and a growing pack is the nest's way of saying it's outgrowing its den.

1719.title: Detardeurus
1719.lore: One of the two adolescent forms guarding Hugel's dragon-nest depths, armored and territorial in the specific way of something that knows it isn't the strongest thing in the caverns yet and is determined not to be tested on the point. Detardeurus holds ground rather than hunts, which the nest wardens read as a good sign — an animal securing borders is an animal that expects to keep living inside them.

1720.title: Hydrolancer
1720.lore: The other adolescent guardian of the Hugel dragon-nest depths, quicker and wetter-elemented than Detardeurus, favoring the caverns' flooded lower galleries where its kin can't easily follow. Hugel's wardens consider a Hydrolancer sighting the reliable early warning that the nest's central clutch — and whatever eventually hatches from it — is close by.

1721.title: Dragon Egg
1721.lore: Unhatched, unmoving, and the single most valuable thing in Hugel's dragon-nest caverns by every measure except the obvious one: nobody who has taken one home has explained afterward what they intended to do with it. The nest's adult guardians treat every egg as equally precious regardless of clutch, which tomb-scholars find more unsettling than reassuring — it suggests the nest itself is keeping count.

2015.title: Dark Pinguicula
2015.lore: The New World's carnivorous flora runs stranger than Midgard's, and the Dark Pinguicula is the strangest common bloom in it — a sticky-leafed trap that doesn't wait for prey to wander in, but leans, slow and deliberate, toward anything warm-blooded that lingers too long at the crossing. Sapha foragers rate it a manageable nuisance. Newcomers rate it the reason they no longer stand still to admire the scenery.

1783.title: Galion
1783.lore: Veins' wild dog packs answer to the factory whistle the way Einbroch's do, but Galion runs leaner and meaner — the alpha temperament of the breed, more territorial than hungry, holding stretches of the ash-fields the way a foreman holds a shift roster. A lone Galion is a nuisance. A Galion that's gathered a pack around it is the reason the mine posts a walk-home escort at all.

1781.title: Drosera
1781.lore: The sundew-flora that carpets Veins' outer fields, sticky-leaved and patient, waiting on the lava-warmed soil for anything careless enough to brush too close. Drosera doesn't hunt so much as accumulate — one plant is harmless, a field of them is a maze where the safe path keeps narrowing the longer you take to find it. The miners route their supply carts around known patches on principle.

1780.title: Muscipular
1780.lore: Veins' largest carnivorous bloom, jaw-leaved and considerably less patient than its sundew cousin Drosera — a Muscipular doesn't wait for prey to wander close, it strikes the moment something warm crosses its reach. The mine posts warning stakes around the densest patches, though the plants have a habit of growing back past the markers within a season.

1917.title: Wounded Morroc
1917.lore: The city is gone. What stands where Morroc used to be is the field form of the thing the party has feared since the shaft under Amon Ra first breathed cold air upward — Satan Morroc, not yet fully risen, wounded by his own arrival into a world too small to hold him comfortably. He is still, somehow, not the worst of what's coming. Killing this form will not be enough. It has never been enough. That was always the point.

1918.title: Incarnation of Morroc
1918.lore: Fragments of Satan Morroc's field-form power, sloughed off and given independent shape as he tears free of the seal that held him — four incarnations, each carrying a splinter of the whole rather than a copy of it. Tomb-guides who study the old dynastic seals recognize the pattern with dread: this is exactly how the deepest chamber's wardens were described breaking apart, generations before anyone thought to write it down as a warning.
